condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, A. Program Institutions: 1. The Borrower, through MoH, shall be responsiblefor the overall implementation and oversight of the Program. To this end, the Borrower, through MoH, shall operate and maintainwithin MoH, throughout Program implementation, a Program Coordination Team (PCT) with a structure, functions, and responsibilitiesacceptable to the World Bank (WB), as set forth in the Operation Manual, including, inter alia: (a) a technical sub-division, and(b) a financial/administrative sub-division.

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, B. Participation Agreements: 1. Prior to carrying out activities with aParticipating Municipality under the Program, the Borrower, through MoH, shall cause the pertinent National Health ServicesEntities to enter into an agreement (“Participation Agreement”) with each of the Participating Municipalities (or, if applicable,amend the existing Participation Agreement), which shall include, inter alia, the Participating Municipality's obligations to carryout the Universal Primary Healthcare program (UPHCP) in accordance with its guidelines and instructions, which shall include theobligations related to the Program, including, inter alia, the ones set forth in the Operation Manual and the Anti-corruptionGuidelines (ACGs).

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, D. Verification Arrangements: 1. The Borrower, through MoH, shall appoint, notlater than three (3) months after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain, throughout Program implementation, one or moreverification agents with experience and qualifications and under terms of reference acceptable to the WB (the “VerificationAgents”) to verify the data and other evidence supporting the achievement(s) of one or more DLIs/DLRs. 2. The Borrower, throughMoH, shall ensure that the Verification Agent referred to in the preceding paragraph shall: (a) carries out the DLIs/DLRsverification process(es) in accordance with the Verification Protocol; and (b) submit to MoH the corresponding verification reportsin a timely manner and in form and substance satisfactory to the WB.

Schedule 2, Section I. Implementation Arrangements, E. Program Action Plan (PAP): The Borrower, through MoH, shall: (a) undertakethe actions set forth in the PAP in a manner satisfactory to the WB; (b) except as the WB and the Borrower, through MoH, shallotherwise agree in writing not to assign, amend, abrogate, or waive, or permit to be assigned, amended, abrogated, or waived, thePAP, or any provision thereof; and (c) maintain policies and procedures adequate to enable it to monitor and evaluate, inaccordance with guidelines acceptable to the WB, the implementation of the PAP.

Schedule 2, Section III. The Borrower, through MoH, shall furnish to the WB each Program Report not later than seventy-five (75)days after the end of each calendar semester, covering the calendar semester.

title.narrative: Participating municipalities that have locally adapted protocols for the inclusive care of LGBTIQA+ people

comment.narrative: Within the ministry, there was an update to the circular that must be used for the development of protocols. Consequently, in order to report this indicator, it was requested to change the reference in the operational definition from 'Circular 21/2012' to a new, more up-to-date Technical Guidance from MINSAL. Since the circular number is explicitly mentioned in the loan agreement, this change will require a restructuring.

title.narrative: Participating municipalities have participated in at least one drill for PHEs and climate change preparedness conducted by Comprehensive Surveillance and Response Teams.

comment.narrative: For 2025, six municipalities participated in simulations; however, none of these have been universalized (DLI1), so they do not count towards the indicator. As a result, the MoH has now committed to scheduling drills for 2026, with clear guidelines on eligible participants and activities, including scenarios such as heat waves and forest fires. The World Bank team has requested to participate in person in at least one of these drills.

title.narrative: Participating municipalities have municipal managers knowledgeable in crucial areas for PHC management

comment.narrative: An initial meeting was held with the municipalities to manage the change regarding this required training. During this meeting, the trainings to be carried out in 2026 were prioritized.

title.narrative: Participating municipalities with interoperability in the electronic clinical record

comment.narrative: Out of the 26 municipalities, at least 3 have already achieved this. A follow-up review with the September cohort is pending, as there has been significant progress in recent months.

title.narrative: Participating municipalities that have a health sectorial plan which includes 'Emergency risk surveillance and preparedness on public health and climate change in universal PHC'
Participating municipalities with positive user experience

comment.narrative: This PDO depends on the completion of the virtual platform (DLI 8.1), as the survey can only be developed and implemented once the application is ready. In the recent mission, it was agreed that, with DLI 8.1 nearing completion, a roadmap will be created to guide the development and rollout of the survey.

title.narrative: Participating municipalities with available healthcare personnel trained in GBV

comment.narrative: During the mission, it was mentioned that the Gender Directorate wants this indicator to be counted as training when participants complete the staff training strategy on 'good treatment of LGBTI+ users.' A consultation was conducted within the Bank with the gender team, and there was no opposition to this more specific change. Therefore, the operational definition will be modified to reflect the needs of the Gender Directorate.

title.narrative: Participating municipalities with a reduction in the percentage of users who do not get a response in <72 hrs when using the TeleSalud portal

comment.narrative: During the mission, various challenges related to this indicator were discussed. Firstly, there is a methodological issue: the annual measurement will result in constantly changing denominators, which needs to be evaluated to determine the most appropriate reporting method. One possibility is to report the indicator using a cohort format. Secondly, this indicator is implemented after the initial years of universalization, meaning that results will be reflected later. A possible restructuring of the indicator was also discussed.

title.narrative: Decrease in the rate of avoidable hospitalizations for PHC patients with multimorbidity in participating municipalities

comment.narrative: There was an attempt to measure the indicator using baseline data from December 2024. However, the number of observations at the community level was very small, as they were limited to ECICEP strategy patients and those with multiple chronic conditions. The rebound effect from COVID-19 also made it necessary to discard this measurement. For reporting purposes, the number of people referred to secondary care was presented, but this does not correspond to the required indicator. To resolve this, a study is underway to deliver formal results and a dashboard by October 2025, which will allow for retrospective reporting with a new baseline. Given these challenges, it is proposed to restructure DLR 3.1 to establish a new baseline and calculation methodology.

title.narrative: Newly registered population at the national level increased

comment.narrative: The baseline for this indicator was supposed to be assessed nationally as of the effectiveness date (September 2023). However, this assessment did not take place. Therefore, changing the date for measurement would require a restructuring. The new baseline would be set as of December 2024, with a value of 1,728,243. By August 2025, the indicator would reach 17.2%. However to be able to report this will part of the restructuring as the definition in the legal agreement includes the baseline from effectiveness date.

title.narrative: People with enhanced resilience to climate risks

comment.narrative: the indicator is determined by the number of individuals from participating municipalities who have taken part in at least one emergency preparedness drill for public health and climate change, organized by the Integrated Surveillance and Response Teams. As of now, given there were no drills this indicator remains at zero.
